title: Doppler Prompting for Stable mmWave-based Human Pose Estimation
claim: Existing sensing systems give jittery predictions under disturbances; ours tracks the stable reference signal more closely.
layout: 3 stacked dashed panels, top-to-bottom, with a disturbance scene between them
description: Three dashed-border panels are stacked vertically. Each panel has a row of five skeleton pose frames above a time-series box. In the box, a green Doppler reference curve is overlaid with a colored prediction curve. Top panel: vision-based HPE in red, with very noisy, erratic fluctuations. Between the top and middle panels sits a scene of a walking person under a ceiling lamp, with shaded light and dark regions and a black occluding box. Red arrows point from the scene to the labels 'Light Mutation' and 'Occlusions'. Middle panel: existing mmWave HPE in blue, which drifts away from the green curve and fluctuates. Bottom panel: PULSE in purple, which hugs the green curve closely and looks smooth. Rounded label boxes on the right name each method and signal type. The eye goes first to the colored curves.
caption: HPE under disturbed inference. Top: Vision-based systems can degrade under illumination shifts and occlusions. Middle: Existing mmWave HPE methods can exhibit inter-frame fluctuations when evaluated over sequences. Bottom: PULSE yields more stable trajectories via controlled Doppler prompting.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) enables privacy-preserving, illumination-robust human pose estimation (HPE), with each mmWave frame represented as a range-angle-Doppler tensor, providing spatial magnitude for localization and Doppler signatures for motion-related cues. However, existing mmWave-based HPE methods either underutilize or naÃ¯vely fuse Doppler signatures with spatial magnitude, disregarding their distinct physical semantics. As a result, non-human Doppler signatures can be misinterpreted as human motion cues, leading to jittery trajectories. We propose PULSE, which converts Doppler signatures into confidence-aware motion prompts and injects them into spatial magnitude reasoning through constrained interactions. By screening Doppler prompts before they influence prediction, PULSE first suppresses spurious spectral motion cues and then uses the screened prompts to stabilize prediction. Across three datasets spanning single- and multi-person settings, PULSE consistently improves pose accuracy and temporal stability, indicating that controlled Doppler prompting is a practical direction for stable mmWave HPE.
